name: Mohamed I. AlHajri
title: Assistant Professor
department: Department of Computer Science and Engineering
lede: Mohamed AlHajri works on learning and inference systems that have to operate inside a budget, whether that budget is measured in bits, in bandwidth, in joules, or in objectives that cannot all be satisfied at once.
bio: He is an Assistant Professor of Computer Science and Engineering at the American University of Sharjah. He completed his PhD at MIT in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, with a minor in Applied Mathematics, in the Claude E. Shannon Communication and Network Group at the Research Laboratory of Electronics.

His doctoral work developed a constrained information exchange message passing algorithm for probabilistic graphical models, asking not only what a node in a network knows but what it is permitted to say. That question, about inference under a communication budget, still runs through most of the group's work today.

Before MIT he read Electrical Engineering at Khalifa University, where he ranked first across the university and graduated on the Dean's Honor List in every semester. Alongside his research he has served in several UAE federal youth bodies and co-directed the IEEE-UAE Distinguished Seminar Series, which drew more than 3,000 registered participants from over 62 countries.

teaching.title: Advanced Machine Learning
teaching.description: Machine learning concepts and data pre-processing, including aggregation, dimensionality reduction, feature selection, and measures of data similarity. Supervised learning with Naive Bayes, SVM, feedforward, convolutional and LSTM networks. Semi-supervised learning including GANs and consistency regularization. Unsupervised methods including K-Medoids, Gaussian mixtures and autoencoders. Ensemble learning and model evaluation.

teaching.title: Modeling and Simulation of Stochastic Systems
teaching.description: Probability and stochastic processes applied to computer engineering: random variables, random processes, queuing models, and discrete-event and discrete-time simulation applied to computer systems and network performance.

teaching.title: Digital Systems
teaching.description: Number systems and the representation of information, Boolean algebra, and the analysis and design of combinational and sequential circuits.
